catalog_locator: pp. 130-131 ('Tones', 'Notes on tones' items 1-4, 'Syllable Structures'); (file named for the preceding paper by Dinh Dien; Zhou's paper)
catalog_quote: There are altogether six tones. Samples of tones are as follows. 1. middle level (33): suɑŋ³³ couple tsuai³³ doze zɑŋ³³ cry, call 2. middle falling (31): vu³¹ mad fu³¹ Buddha ju³¹ high 3. low rising (24): duŋ²⁴ salty, salted dzuŋ²⁴ tired ʔiu²⁴ bamboo 4. low falling-rising (214): khuai²¹⁴ hurry ... 5. middle rising (35): ... 6. high falling (42): tsɿ⁴² one ... Notes on tones: 1. The middle level tone is usually as high as 44. 2. Sometimes the low falling-rising tone and the high rising tone can be mixed. For some words, it is usually difficult for both the informant and the investigator to determine whether it is 214 or 35. But in most cases, the tone value between these two can be clearly distinguished. 3. The tone of some noun prefixes are usually pronounced so weak that it is difficult to determine their tone values, therefore we can record them as zero (0), e.g. vu⁰no³⁵ bird pə⁰qu²⁴ skin lə⁰zo³¹lə⁰ze³³ speckle qə⁰tɕu³¹ rimple. [p. 131] 4. There are no tone categories for modern Chinese loan words, the tones of modern Chinese loan words are classified under such tones as the mid-level (33), the low-falling (31), the high-falling (42), and the low-rising (24) respectively. Syllable Structures. A syllable in Judu Gelao language is usually formed by an initial consonant + a final + a tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Judu (White/Duoluo) Gelao is a six-tone language in which every full syllable carries a lexical tone; the author gives no word-stress rule. The only prominence asymmetry described is that noun-class prefixes (vu-, pə-, lə-, qə-) are prosodically weak, toneless minor syllables (written tone 0) preceding the full-toned root, i.e. prefixed words are weak-strong (root-prominent).
new_statements.exceptions: Weakness is stated only for 'some noun prefixes'; modern Chinese loans are assigned to tones 33/31/42/24; tones 214 and 35 are sometimes hard to distinguish.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms from elicited fieldwork data (1999); no phrase-level prosody discussed. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the paper.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes the Judu 居都 village variety (Liuzhi Special District, Guizhou; ~400 speakers in 1999), whose speakers call themselves to³¹ʔlo³⁵ = Duoluo/Telue, i.e. White Gelao; Glottolog whit1267 'Duoluo Gelao' [giw] covers Judu, Moji (Longlin, Guangxi), Malipo (Yunnan) and Ha Giang (Vietnam) White Gelao. Glottolog lists the author as 'Zhuo, Guoyan' (ref 117770); the paper header reads Zhou Guoyan 周国炎, Central University for Nationalities. The SEAlang PDF is misnamed Zhou's paper is its pp. 9-17).

tone_statements.quote: 仡佬语各方言点塞音韵尾消失，已没有舒声调和促声调之分。弯桃声调有 3 个，另有 33、24 两个声调只出现在汉借词中；居都 3 个，月亮湾 3 个，高调都有高升、高平二读；越南同文 3 个，中平调 33 调有 32 调变体，多出现在词头、叠音词中。 … 弯桃的 55 调、居都的 33 调、月亮湾的 33 调、同文的 33 调有较整齐的对应，但居都小部分读 45 调；弯桃的 31 调、居都的 31 调、月亮湾的 35、55 调、同文的 55 调有比较整齐的对应；弯桃的 35 调、居都的 45 调对应月亮湾的 31 调、同文的 31 调。
tone_statements.translation: In every Gelao dialect stop codas are lost and unchecked vs checked tones are no longer distinguished. Wantao has 3 tones, plus 33 and 24 found only in Chinese loans; Judu 3, Yueliangwan 3, in both the high tone reads either high-rising or high-level; Tongwen (Vietnam) 3, its mid-level 33 having a 32 variant mostly in prefixes and reduplications. … Wantao 55, Judu 33, Yueliangwan 33, Tongwen 33 correspond regularly, but a small part of Judu reads 45; Wantao 31, Judu 31, Yueliangwan 35/55, Tongwen 55 correspond regularly; Wantao 35 and Judu 45 correspond to Yueliangwan 31 and Tongwen 31.
tone_statements.locator: p. 29 (first paragraph, tone correspondence table and last lines) continuing to p. 30; sec. 一 语音比较, 1. 声调比较及演变特点
tone_statements.summary: Three tones in Judu Gelao on root morphemes: mid level 33, falling 31 and high 45 (heard rising or level); checked tones merged after loss of stop codas; old checked syllables now read 45.

tone_statements.quote: In this section we will describe the tonal systems of three Gelao varieties: Laozhai, Qiaoshang and Wanzi. These varieties represent three Gelao branches and constitute a main basis for the reconstruction of Proto-Gelao in Chapter 4. 3.10.1. Laozhai variety. The Laozhai variety has four tones: /45/, /35/, /31/, and /33/. … Laozhai Gelao only splits tone A, based on voicing opposition of initials: tone /45/ occurs with the voiceless series and tone /35/ occurs with the voiced series.
tone_statements.summary: Laozhai (Malipo, Duoluo/Southwestern) Gelao has four tones, 45, 35, 31, 33, from the author's fieldwork; A1/A2 split by initial voicing; 45 lowers to 35 after another syllable. Judu not treated.

sources.note: First-hand fieldwork (Judu village, Liuzhi, 1999). Describes 53 initials, 29 finals, six tones (33, 31, 24, 214, 35, 42), syllable = initial + final + tone. Never uses the words stress/accent. Only prominence-related statement (p.130, Notes on tones 3): noun prefixes are 'pronounced so weak' that their tone cannot be determined and are written with tone 0 (vu0 no35 'bird', pe0 qu24 'skin', qe0 tcu31 'rimple') -- i.e. a weak/toneless minor syllable before a full-toned root.
